yt_posts.topic: Kaspa: the 1.4 cent bottom that never came
yt_posts.body_style: thesis-first with the receipt chain behind it
yt_posts.engagement_question: If Kaspa never sees 1.4 cents, are you buying here at 2.9, or are you still waiting for a number that is not coming?
yt_posts.body:
Everybody had 1.4 cents circled on the Kaspa chart. That was the number. That was where the four year cycle crowd said we were going, and honestly, a few weeks ago I could not have told you they were wrong.

We never got there.

Here is what happened instead. Bitcoin went from 62k to 79k in a single week, wicked to 79,989, which is eleven dollars away from 80,000, and then took it clean this morning at 81,257. Roughly 25 percent in seven days, in a month that is usually red and especially unkind in a midterm year.

Now run the October bottom thesis against that. For that bottom to land, we have to break back below the support we just built, get under 57k, and then keep falling to the 0.786 at 40k that everybody keeps pointing at. In five to nine weeks. September has not even started. That does not happen without something genuinely catastrophic, and a stock market retracement does not count, because we are already expecting one.

I was 10 percent open to the idea that the bottom lands after October. I am not anymore.

On Kaspa specifically, the setup changed while everyone was arguing. There is a higher low forming against a lower low, which is a bullish divergence, and Kaspa is still sitting way below its 50-week SMA. It held up through this bear market better than almost anything else I own, and it is at 2.9 cents right now.

I am not pretending I am in profit. Most of my money went into Kaspa at 11 cents. I am also not selling any of it, because nothing about why I bought it has changed. And for the first time in a long stretch the data is pointing our way: ISM PMI crossed above 50 in January for the first time in over four years, hit 55 in May, and printed 57 in July. Crypto lags that. It always has.

The risks are real: new Iran sanctions dragging the S&P and NASDAQ down, 50 percent auto tariffs threatened on Canada, a possible September government shutdown, and a Fed rate decision mid month where a hike is not off the table.

But none of that is the bottom. The bottom may already be behind us, and the people still posting a decimal point at 1.4 cents have not updated a single thing since June.

So here is what I actually want to know: if Kaspa never sees 1.4 cents, are you buying here at 2.9, or are you still waiting for a number that is not coming?

Hit like and subscribe if you would rather be early on the turn than argue about it afterwards.

yt_posts.topic: The 27 million ceiling: listings decide market cap
yt_posts.engagement_question: Which Robinhood chain coin do you think lands on the app next, and more importantly, why that one?
yt_posts.body:
Pipe Dog is a dog with a pipe. It is sitting at 27 million dollars. Artificial Inu is sitting at 27 million dollars. Stonk Brokers is sitting at 27 million dollars.

Kitsu is Vlad Tenev's actual dog. 1.9 million.

I kept staring at this trying to work out what those three have that Kitsu does not, because it is not the art, it is not the community, and it is definitely not the concept. A dog with a pipe is not a better idea than the Robinhood CEO's real Shiba.

It is the listings. Every one of the 27 million dollar tokens is on CoinMarketCap with centralized exchanges behind it. Pipe Dog alone is on twelve of them. Kitsu has neither, and it is grinding along under two million on a chart that is actually holding a clean floor.

Once you see it you cannot unsee it. Market cap in this corner of crypto is not a referendum on quality. It is a function of how many places a normal person can click buy. A team that knows how to get listed will outrun a better token every single time, and that is not a complaint, it is the filter.

Which is exactly what happened to me with Cooper. I sold mine at a rest stop on the drive back to New York. The office dog at Robinhood was a genuinely good concept and the team did nothing during the single best week crypto has had all year: no content, no push, just status updates telling us they never manipulate the chart. Whoever took profits near the top got a 6x from 50k to 300k. If they had spent that week getting listed instead of posting updates, we would be having a very different conversation.

Base Cat is the counterexample. It launched on August 15, hit Coinbase's listing roadmap on the 21st, and started spot trading on the 24th. Nine days. It dumped right after the alert fired, which is its own lesson about buying an announcement, but the listing is what put it on the map at all.

So this is the filter I am running on Robinhood chain plays now. Not which one has the best meme. Which one has a team capable of putting it in front of retail before retail knows it exists. Cash Cat already did it. I think Tendies gets there. What If has the loudest community on that chain and no listings yet, which is either the opportunity or the warning depending on how you read it.

The whole degen edge is buying the token that is going to get listed, before it gets listed.

So which Robinhood chain coin do you think lands on the app next, and more importantly, why that one?

Like and subscribe if you would rather learn the pattern than chase the pump.
